title: Pressures on future food supply
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:52Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Pressures on future food supply
card: Food supply is how much food can be grown and delivered. Several pressures may reduce it in future.
a rise in global temperatures that can change rainfall and bring more heat waves, droughts and floods. These can lower crop yields (how much a crop produces from a set area) and harm livestock.
farms need water to grow crops and raise animals. If rivers, dams or groundwater run low, farmers can grow less.
cities growing outwards can cover farmland with houses and roads. That land can no longer grow food.
draft.remember: Hotter, drier weather, less water and less farmland can all cut the food that can be grown.

a.q: Which change is an example of urban spread threatening food supply?
opts: New suburbs are built over market gardens
A dam on a river holds less water each year
Heat waves cause wheat crops to produce less
Farmers sell more of their crops overseas
a.why: Houses and roads built over market gardens mean that land can no longer grow food. The dam is a water shortage and the heat waves are a climate change effect. Selling crops overseas does not remove farmland.
a.clue: Which one takes farmland away by covering it?

b.q: Rainfall has fallen for years around a town in Western Australia, and the local dams are low. Farmers there now irrigate fewer paddocks. Which pressure on food supply is this most directly?
b.why: Farmers can irrigate fewer paddocks because the dams hold too little water, so this is a water shortage. Climate change may be one cause of the lower rainfall, but the problem farmers face directly is the lack of water.
b.clue: What do the farmers lack to irrigate their paddocks?

a.best: New suburbs are built over market gardens
